title: What of those Godpossibled souls that we nightly impossibilise
html_source:
A condemnation of contraception. A major theme of this chapter is the slaying of the sacred oxen, i.e. the obstruction of the practice of generating human offspring. What seems to be condemned here is the preoccupation of young Irishmen, represented by Stephen and his medical-student friends, with drinking and protected sex.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: I’m not sure this is a ‘condemnation’, only becaue it’s difficult to determine whose voice speaks this; and because Joyce certainly wouldn’t have cared to condemn contraception. This is very decently done though.

(I think it’s not just to do with protected sex but also with masturbation.)
